newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended a grim Thursday down for the fourth consecutive session, hit by a wave of negative sentiment that has sent prices tumbling, dealers said.
The market is worried over confusing signals from government and the Reserve Bank on scrapping exchange controls and rising fears of an interest rate hike.
A recent spate of poor results from groups like retailer Edgars and Coke bottler ABI has added to the gloom.
"All the sentiment is negative. No one can see any positive news on the horizon," said one dealer.

The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) has suffered badly in the wake of the most recent rand collapse. In quieter periods the JSE tends to track Wall Street, but the market is now steadfastly focused on its domestic hard times and has ignored record breaking surges in New York.

As trades flowed through after the close of trade the all-share index climbed a little from its day lows, but still ended at 6,802.9, down 71.0 points, as industrials slid to 8,014.4, down 77.1 points.
Dealers said they were nervously watching out for October gold and foreign exchange reserve data due at 1600 GMT. There is fear the recent speculation on the rand may have weakened reserves further.
"I don't think they are going to provide any positive news and that's the consensus feeling," one dealer said.
But some traders held that the market may be in for a much-needed pleasent surprise. "I think people are being too pessimistic," another dealer said.

The day saw blood spilled in most major stocks with De Beers ending the day down 425 cents at 134.00 rand, a drop of nearly three percent. The stock was also hit by fears over the renewal of a Russian diamond deal.
South African Breweries shed 75 cents to 119.50 rand and Anglos lost 375 cents to 277.50 rand.
Gold shares, which were resilient earlier in the week, suffered a second bad day running. The golds index fell nine points to 1,693.0 over ears on a jittery bullion price.
Western Deep Levels dropped 150 cents to 147.50 rand, Kloof lost 75 cents to 40.50 rand and Vaal Reefs dipped 250 cents to 352.50 rand.

Futures traders were active in the spot market and futures contracts also dipped. The all-share December contract was at 6,200/20 from 6,265 as industrials dropped to 7,656/70 from 7,795 and golds retreated to 1212/15 from 1,224.
